### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/field.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0cd594b3c77d7e5ac5be02b4c284c5ad5cd1009c`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/field.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 42 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0cd594b3c77d7e5ac5be02b4c284c5ad5cd1009c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `122f6d362b840cdeb4086fd23e8bb6b9ba7c57ad` — the merge of head `0fc9219463f11e3dd2e96d3de52ce83ace19649f` into base `0cd594b3c77d7e5ac5be02b4c284c5ad5cd1009c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 122f6d362b840cdeb4086fd23e8bb6b9ba7c57ad && git checkout 122f6d362b840cdeb4086fd23e8bb6b9ba7c57ad
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0cd594b3c77d7e5ac5be02b4c284c5ad5cd1009c 0fc9219463f11e3dd2e96d3de52ce83ace19649f && git checkout -B drift-repro 0cd594b3c77d7e5ac5be02b4c284c5ad5cd1009c && git merge --no-ff 0fc9219463f11e3dd2e96d3de52ce83ace19649f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0cd594b3c77d7e5ac5be02b4c284c5ad5cd1009c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0cd594b3c77d7e5ac5be02b4c284c5ad5cd1009c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0fc9219463f11e3dd2e96d3de52ce83ace19649f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/data/currency-config-record-mode.test.ts (pins the refusal set), packages/spec/liveness/field.json (the two dated NARROWED notes), .changeset/31958-summary-currency-outside-admitted-rollup.md (the Clause-② and Metadata-protocol declarations); the three regenerated pages content/docs/references/data/field.mdx, content/docs/references/data/object.mdx and content/docs/references/system/migration.mdx are generated output, read as the describe text's carrier and not reviewed. Read, never reviewed: docs/adr/0144-multi-currency-record-currency-dated-rates-write-time-home-projection.md (D6 and its 2026-11-09 note), packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts (sourceFieldMeta), packages/services/service-analytics/src/measure-currency-coherence.ts, packages/objectql/src/record-currency-aggregate-door.ts (recordCurrencySummaryRefusal), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (the metadata_spec_invalid path), packages/objectql/src/engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts (relation resolution), ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/SummaryField.tsx, skills/**, and the census over examples/**, packages/**, ui/**, content/docs/**, docs/ and skills/.

Inputs: card #31958 (body, triage 6744552807, claim 6745949455, claim amend 1 6746006322, os-dev report 6748838333, claim amend 2 6748867166), PR #31976 body and file list, the net diff of `0fc92194` against `main` `0cd594b3` (the merge base; nine files, +383/-26), and the check-runs on `0fc92194`: every run is `success` or a path-filtered `skipped` (Lint UI, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, UI Published Artifacts, the Dogfood shards, the queue verdicts, the opt-in harnesses); none failed. Nothing was built, run or re-run here.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set change the diff implies, each judged against claim amend 1 (the ruling) and ADR-0144 D6 as amended:

- **Object door, `refuseUnadmittedSummaryCurrency` (object.zod.ts), wired into `ObjectSchemaBase`'s `superRefine` beside `refuseDishonestRecordCurrencyField`.** Judged on `type: 'summary'` fields carrying a `currencyConfig` object, at `['fields', NAME, 'currencyConfig']`:
  - a `count` roll-up refuses every mode (`record`, `fixed`, `dynamic`) — **right**, the ruling's first bullet verbatim;
  - `dynamic`, written or materialised from an absent `currencyMode` (`CurrencyConfigSchema` defaults it, so `{}` reaches the refinement as `'dynamic'`; the `?? 'dynamic'` fallback covers a raw map too) — **right**, the ruling refuses `dynamic` on every summary. The message's premise ("no reader draws a roll-up in the tenant default currency") holds in the live tree: `SummaryField.tsx` reads no `currencyConfig`, and `sourceFieldMeta` relays `defaultCurrency` only under `fixed` and `currencyField` only under `record`;
  - `record` on a summary with no `summaryOperations` naming a child object and field — **right**: the admitted roll-up reads a child amount, so this is "not admitted" from the object alone. A `record` on a sum/min/max/avg with a child named is left to the stack — **right**, the object cannot see the child;
  - `fixed` on sum / min / max / avg — **accepted, unchanged**, as the ruling orders; verified that `plugin.ts` relays the `fixed` code for any field type and `assertMeasureCurrenciesCoherent` consumes it.
  - `refuseDishonestRecordCurrencyField` now skips a `count` roll-up's `record` pointer so the field carries one issue, not two — **right**, the whole config is refused by the new door and the pointer's target is moot.
- **Stack door, case (c) inside `collectRecordCurrencyPathErrors` (stack.zod.ts), no third collector.** `judgeRecord` is true only for a `record` summary on a declared parent, over a declared child whose field the stack holds. The five refusals — child amount with its own (one-segment) code field, `fixed` child amount (prescribing that fixed spelling), child amount with no currency, child amount following another object through its `master_detail`, roll-up written (`relationshipField`) through another relation than the one the child amount follows — are each a roll-up D6's amended note refuses ("admitted only through that very `master_detail` field"; every other roll-up "is refused as the first bullet says"). **Right, and no wider than the ruling:** the admitted shape's branch (`summaryCurrency.currencyField === amount.code` → continue) is byte-for-byte #31956's, so the admitted roll-up still parses; the (b) finding for a `fixed` / mis-pointed `record` over a following child is unchanged; the skips (undeclared parent or child, extension-only child, child field not held, unresolvable relation) are exactly #31956's skip rules extended to (c).
- **Not narrowed, verified:** `CurrencyConfigSchema`, a standalone `FieldSchema` and `ObjectExtensionSchema.fields` call none of the currency doors (the only call sites are the object `superRefine` at object.zod.ts:4305 and `validateCrossReferences`), so they parse what they parsed; `currency` and `formula` fields are untouched. A `fixed` roll-up over a child amount with its own code field is not judged at the spec — **right**: `recordCurrencySummaryRefusal` refuses every summary over a record-mode child amount at registration, whatever the summary declares, and the test pins that this pass does not repeat it.
- **Public surface.** No export, key or type moves: the diff is the describe text of `FieldSchema.currencyConfig` plus the `CurrencyConfigSchema` docblock; `api-surface/` and `authorable-surface/` are untouched and `check:generated` is inside the green Lint & Repo Gates run. The three `content/docs/references` pages carry the new describe text only.
- **Census.** Independently re-counted on the head: 470 `Field.summary(` / `type: 'summary'` sites plus 5 YAML `type: summary` snippets outside `content/docs/references`, `CHANGELOG`, `dist` and `releases` (the dev's 480 differs by include set, not by substance). Of the files holding both a summary site and `currencyConfig`, only `currency-config-record-mode.test.ts` puts a `currencyConfig` on a summary — the two #31956 admitted pins. `examples/app-showcase` (`invoice`, `project`), `content/docs/data-modeling/*`, `common-patterns.mdx`, `skills/**` and the objectql/formula/dogfood fixtures carry none. **0 fixes owed is credible and verified.**
- **Liveness.** `field.json` moves two `note` strings only (`summaryOperations`, `currencyConfig`), each a dated NARROWED entry naming the ruling record and the two doors; `status`, `evidence` and verdicts unchanged; both rows are in `undrilled-containers.baseline.json`, and the Spec property liveness run is green. **Right.**
- **Skills-docs: none** — verified: no `currencyConfig` is taught near a `summary` anywhere under `skills/**`; the parent-path teaching is follow-up #31957, as the changeset says.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/spec': minor` with the `fix(spec)!:` title and a **BREAKING** banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on both the PR body and the changeset, `Skills-docs: none` with its reason, and `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its why. This matches what the diff publishes: nothing is widened (no new key, export or value), and an accept set is narrowed, which the repo spells as a `minor` breaking narrowing (precedent `30093-page-sort-unknown-field.md`; `check-changeset-no-major` refuses `major` outright). The Check Changeset run is green. The `Clause-②:` arm is the gate's spelling of the claim's bare `no`, restated by the seat in claim amend 2 — consistent. The adr-0087 disposition is gate-consistent (the body carries "What an author does" prose and no FROM/TO prescription) and precedent-consistent (`29304`, `30093`); see ④ nit 4 for the one leg that admits a mechanical rewrite.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Face.** The brief named the narrowing face; `reviewFace` reads the **schema** face off the committed paths (`field.zod.ts`, `object.zod.ts`, `stack.zod.ts` are `hits`). Both map to CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER; this record is stamped at that tier with the `Scope:` line the schema face asks for (hits + implementing files), widened to the narrowing floor (every non-prose path of the diff).
- **Dev deviation 1 (Clause-② spelling)** — answered: claim amend 2 restates the claim line as `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; PR body and changeset carry it verbatim.
- **Dev deviation 2 (#31956 pin re-pointed)** — answered: the `dynamic` half of "names the mode a roll-up declared instead" now asserts the object issue, because `defineStack` parses `objects` through `ObjectSchema` before `validateCrossReferences`, so `dynamic` cannot reach the stack pass. The file is inside the claim's surface. Accepted.
- **Dev deviation 3 (dogfood battery ran)** — owed by the `(narrowing)` arm; the Dogfood Regression Gate run is green. Accepted.
- **Out-of-scope finding (b)'s `dynamic` message branch dead through `defineStack`** — answered as ④ nit 1.
- **Out-of-scope finding extensions not judged** — answered: consistent with every currency door (none runs on `ObjectExtensionSchema`); a count with a currency added by an extension still parses, as the test pins. Accepted deviation, no card owed.
- **Out-of-scope finding stored rows keep registering** — answered: `registry.ts`'s `[metadata_spec_invalid]` path logs and badges rather than gates, so a stored refused summary registers with `_diagnostics` and is refused on its next save. Consistent with every spec narrowing. Accepted.
- `open_questions: []` — none to escalate. No security findings.
- The commit-status API reports `pending` with zero statuses; that is the legacy statuses surface with nothing posted, not a check-run, and does not count against the head.

### ④ Design judgment

Read against the published spec on `main` `0cd594b3`: the `FieldSchema.currencyConfig` describe text declares the config "for a currency field, for a formula field whose returnType is currency, and for a summary that rolls up, through a master_detail, child amounts that follow this record's currency … Absent: dynamic mode." No other `currencyConfig` on a `summary` was ever declared; it parsed because the one config shape is shared across field types. So the narrowing takes no declared capability away at the consumer. For `record` it makes the spec's own refusal real: D6's first bullet, kept by the amended note for "a `summary` over a child amount that has its own code field, or one that rolls up through any other relation", already refuses those roll-ups at registration (`recordCurrencySummaryRefusal`); the spec now refuses the declaration that labelled such a total with a currency it is not in. For `count`, a currency on a row count is wrong for every reader. For `dynamic`, the one reader chain that could consume it relays nothing under that mode, and an absent config still parses, so an author loses no behaviour. The one mode a reader consumes on a summary, `fixed`, stays accepted — the ruling's and the brief's "a read mode is not inert" rule, honoured. The refusal set matches claim amend 1 exactly, no wider, and each refusal names its remedy.

Attempts to break it, each read in the cited code:

- An admitted roll-up with `record` naming the parent's code → still parses (the unchanged continue). A `record` summary whose pointer names a non-code sibling → refused by the one-segment check in `refuseDishonestRecordCurrencyField`, and when the child's path code is not a code field (a) tells it once at the amount — no gap, no double count.
- A `record` sum whose child amount follows this parent through `master_detail` A while the roll-up is written through lookup B → refused by the new relation branch; written through A → admitted. Correct reading of "that very `master_detail` field".
- `currencyConfig: {}` on a sum → materialised `dynamic`, refused at the object; the test pins it.
- A `count` with `record` → one issue (the count leg), the pointer skip holds.
- An extension adding a count with a currency → parses, by design of every door; the stack's (c) skips an extension-only child too. Consistent.

Findings (no must-fix, no should-fix):

- **nit 1** — (b)'s `dynamic` message branch in `collectRecordCurrencyPathErrors` is unreachable through `defineStack` now that the object door refuses `dynamic` first; left in place because the pass's input is not typed as parsed. No effect on correctness or the contract. Accepted deviation (dev's acceptance note 5).
- **nit 2** — a `record` roll-up whose relation the pass cannot resolve (no `relationshipField`, several relations back), or whose `summaryOperations.field` the declared child does not hold, parses at both doors. These are #31956's skip rules carried into (c); the engine resolves the relation at registration. A spec refusal of an ambiguous or dangling roll-up would be a narrowing of its own, outside this card. Follow-up card at most; no fix here.
- **nit 3** — `fixed` on a `summary` with no `summaryOperations` is accepted. The ruling enumerates sum / min / max / avg and says nothing of a roll-up with no operations; accepting it narrows nothing beyond the ruling and nothing reads it. Accepted deviation.
- **nit 4** — the `dynamic` leg admits a mechanical rewrite (delete the key; the engine drew nothing from it), which a semantic migration entry could carry; the `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` disposition is nevertheless gate-consistent and matches the narrowing precedents, and the refusal text names the remedy. Accepted deviation; a follow-up card if the migrations ledger wants the deletion recorded.
- **nit 5** (prose face) — the census figure 480 is not reproducible to the unit (475 here); the material claim — two `currencyConfig` declarations on summaries, both the admitted pins, zero fixes — is verified exactly. No fix.

Nits alone end the round.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：汇总字段（summary）上的 `currencyConfig`，凡不在 ADR-0144 允许的汇总写法之内，现在在对象级和 stack 级检查都会被明确拒绝：
  - `count` 汇总：任何币种模式都拒绝（计数不是金额）；
  - sum/min/max/avg：`dynamic` 拒绝；`record` 只允许 #31956 落地的那种（沿 master_detail 汇总、明细金额跟随主记录币种），其余拒绝；
  - `fixed` 保留（分析服务确实读它）。
- 为什么改：这些写法今天能解析，但没有任何读取方会照着它显示，属于“写了也不生效”的假承诺（#31956 复核时发现，另开 #31958）。
- 风险与回滚：这是收紧，changeset 标了 minor 和 BREAKING，并带迁移说明。复核方重新数了全仓 475 处汇总字段，只有 2 处写了 `currencyConfig`，都是允许的写法，需要改的是 0 处。回滚就是 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` 的 `refuseUnadmittedSummaryCurrency`，以及 `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` 的 `collectRecordCurrencyPathErrors` 新增的 (c) 段。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/data/currency-config-record-mode.test.ts`，应全绿。
- 需要你做的：无。本 PR 不属受管面，契约复核已通过，由本席落地。
- 席位意见：建议合。CI 全绿，契约复核 PASS，无应改项，5 个 nit 都不需要改代码。
